top_story_html:
TOP STORY

A record-breaking $6.3 billion hack, a tech-driven market wobble, and a surprisingly strong earnings season for the biggest public crypto companies all landed in the same 48 hours.

stories.headline: Binance Sets Aside $6.34 Billion to Cover Hack Losses
stories.body:
Binance CEO Richard Teng said the exchange has earmarked $6.34 billion to cover losses from what's being called the largest hack in crypto history, telling users 'your assets are safe.' Teng said the attacker used a self-destruct mechanism paired with an EIP-7702 delegation that bypassed Binance's normal approval controls.

Covering the full shortfall from company funds is the responsible move, and it's a notably different posture than past exchange collapses where users were left holding the bag. Still, the size of the number is a reminder that 'too big to hack' was never actually true for anyone.

stories.headline: Blockchain Sleuths Pin the Hack on North Korea's TraderTraitor
stories.body:
Chainalysis and TRM Labs have linked the $6.3 billion Binance hack to North Korea's TraderTraitor group, the same actors blamed for the Bybit hack earlier.

At this point North Korean state hackers targeting crypto exchanges feels less like breaking news and more like a recurring weather pattern. The bigger question isn't attribution, it's why the industry keeps building systems these groups can still find a way into.

stories.headline: The Ethereum Upgrade That May Have Amplified the Damage
stories.body:
Security experts told Cointelegraph that attackers could likely have drained Binance's wallets without EIP-7702, but the Ethereum upgrade may have helped bypass withdrawal safeguards and widen the losses.

EIP-7702 was built to make wallets more flexible and user-friendly, not to open new attack surface, but this is the classic tradeoff of giving smart-contract powers to ordinary accounts. Expect every exchange's security team to be re-reading their delegation permissions this week.

stories.headline: Bitcoin Eyes Its Worst October in 12 Years
stories.body:
Bitcoin circled $77,000 as crypto markets navigated a broader US stock-market downside, while gold also fell to its lowest price in a year, per Cointelegraph.

When bitcoin and gold are falling together, it's less a story about crypto-specific fear and more about a market-wide appetite for risk assets shrinking all at once. Worth watching whether that correlation holds or breaks as the hack fallout settles.

stories.headline: Strategy Posts $19.5 Billion Q3 Net Income, Moves to Daily Preferred Dividends
stories.body:
Strategy reported $19.53 billion in Q3 net income on a $20.91 billion bitcoin gain, now holds 848,517 BTC, and shifted its preferred shares to daily dividends, per The Block.

A headline number that size is easy to be dazzled by, but it's really an accounting reflection of bitcoin's own price swings rather than operating performance. The daily dividend structure change is the more interesting detail for anyone tracking how sustainable this balance-sheet strategy actually is.

stories.headline: Coinbase Swings to $719 Million Q3 Profit
stories.body:
Coinbase reported third-quarter net income of $719 million, driven largely by gains on its crypto holdings, while revenue held flat at $1.22 billion, according to Decrypt.

Flat revenue paired with a big profit number tells you where the gains actually came from, the balance sheet, not new business growth. It's a fine quarter, but one worth reading past the headline figure.

stories.headline: SEC Charges Two Firms Over $130 Million Crypto Trading Scheme
stories.body:
The SEC has charged two companies with defrauding investors of over $130 million through a crypto Ponzi-like scheme, according to Bitcoin Magazine.

Enforcement actions like this rarely make the splashiest headlines, but they're the slow, unglamorous work that actually protects people from the next scheme. The hack dominates the news cycle, but fraud charges like this are the quieter, equally persistent threat.

stories.headline: Zcash Grants Group Offers $124 Million Compromise Amid Governance Backlash
stories.body:
Zcash Community Grants proposed redirecting about $124 million in existing and future funding toward mining rewards, but critics say the plan fails to address underlying governance and accountability concerns, per Cointelegraph.

Throwing money at a governance dispute rarely settles the governance dispute. If critics are right that this sidesteps accountability questions rather than answering them, expect the backlash to keep simmering regardless of the dollar figure attached.

missed_story.headline: Hacker Accidentally Nukes a Random 2017 Token by 90%
missed_story.body: In the middle of moving billions in stolen funds, the Binance hacker reportedly dumped a little-known token from 2017, and the token promptly crashed 90 percent. It's a strange little footnote to a record-breaking theft: even criminals holding a nine-figure haul can tank an obscure altcoin just by touching it. A small reminder of how thin liquidity really is once you look past the big-cap names.
